> I'm not sure if I revere him but I do think he's cool.  His Manifesto
> is just an incredible work, though many try to discredit it by
> describing it as "rambling and incoherent," or dismissing his
> reasoning by comparing it to something a college sophomore or even
> freshman might write.  I'm hardly an intellectual but I know what I
> like and I like it.  My favorite bits are what he writes about
> leftists.  I had never liked leftists to begin with, but St. Ted
> finally gave me a comprehensive insight into their frame of mind.
> As for the evils of technology, George Orwell and Aldous Huxley
> already had predicted much of what Ted describes, so those parts
> of the Manifesto might not be that original.  Whether you disagree
> with the Manifesto, you can't dismiss it as the incoherent
> rantings of a schizophrenic; it is extremely well-written and
> very organized in its presentation, hardly what one would expect
> from a schizophrenic.
